From: Samantha Li <samantha@codehub.org>

Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Stewardship Support Request: OpenStitch Mini-Sprint (Dec)

Hi David,

Hope you’re well — I’m Samantha, one of the organizers for OpenStitch. We’re running a focused mini-sprint for maintainers and contributors on Dec 10–12 (virtual + two regional in-person hubs). Historically these events are small but high-value: ~100–150 attendees, lots of short modeling workshops and pair programming.

We’re requesting stewardship support in the form of platform credits and a short trial extension so a subset of maintainers can run heavier inference jobs during the sprint (small model fine-tuning + evaluation runs). Attached is our initial ask and a simple budget (sponsorship-ask.pdf, budget.csv).

What we’d love from Redwood:
- 60k token-equivalent credits (to cover compute for workshops and demos)
- a 14–21 day trial extension for three maintainer accounts to allow pre-event testing and immediate post-event follow-ups

We’re happy to include Redwood in event materials, social posts, and a short post-event writeup (200–300 words). If you need any more underwriting details or an attendee breakdown, I can send that over.

Thanks for considering — appreciate the support for maintainers.

Best,
Samantha Li
OpenStitch Organizer
samantha@codehub.org
https://openstitch.dev

Attachments: sponsorship-ask.pdf (PDF), budget.csv (CSV)

Hi Samantha — thanks for the note and the attachments. Looks like a great program. A couple quick clarifying questions so we can scope the credit and extension properly:

1) Expected peak concurrent users and rough per-session token budget (so we can model peak latency/cost).
2) Will the maintainer accounts be using dedicated GPUs or mostly smaller hosted runs?
3) Do you need any special data handling (e.g., private datasets, air-gapped materials) during the sprint?

High-level, I can provision a provisional stewardship allocation while Marissa reviews the sponsorship ask and Karthik checks quota/ledgers. Provisionally we could do 50k tokens + a 14-day trial extension for up to 3 accounts, pending final approval and a short post-event summary that confirms usage and a one-paragraph testimonial.

Can you also fill out this short intake form (https://drive.google.com/openstitch-mini-sprint-ask) — it helps our finance/compliance teams capture the right metadata.

If that provisional amount looks good, I’ll loop in Marissa and Karthik to fast-track approval.

— David

Thanks David — quick answers below and I attached a pared-down ask (openstitch-revised-ask.pdf) with a clearer usage plan.

- Attendees: we expect ~120 active contributors; of those ~25 will participate in heavier model runs during workshops.
- Peak concurrent heavy users: ~12.
- Typical session: 10–30 minute runs; for the workshops we expect several dozens of short runs to evaluate model outputs and a handful of longer evaluation jobs.
- Compute profile: mostly hosted smaller runs (gpt-style families), a couple of short local fine-tune jobs for maintainers (we’ll keep any private data out of Redwood unless explicitly approved).

We’ll include Redwood branding in event slides, mention in the post-event wrap (200 words), and can provide a usage report within 10 business days after the sprint. The revised ask includes a slightly higher peak allowance and a clearer breakout for workshop vs demo usage.

Let me know if the provisional 50k + 14-day extension will work while you route approvals. Appreciate the quick help.
